# AMD Showcases 6th Gen AMD EPYC Processors to Lead Next Era of AI and Enterprise Computing 

 Published November 10, 2026 

 

 AMD announced the general availability of 6th Gen EPYC server SP7 processors in November 2026. 6th Gen EPYC data center CPUs provide a foundation for growing agentic AI deployments and demanding enterprise applications. (Credit: AMD) 

 If you have any questions regarding the terms and conditions of this Agreement, please contact the AMD Law Department at amd.trademarks@amd.com. 

News Highlights:

- 6th Gen AMD EPYC SP7 CPU-based platforms are now shipping from leading server OEMs and ODMs.
- 6th Gen EPYC CPUs are expected to power cloud instances across all major, global cloud service providers, with recent announcements from Microsoft Azure and OCI showcasing leadership agent orchestration, concurrent agent sandboxes, as well as web and enterprise applications.
- Powered by the new AMD “Zen 6” architecture, 6th Gen EPYC CPUs deliver a broad portfolio of workload-optimized server CPUs spanning agentic AI, enterprise, cloud computing, HPC and general-purpose computing.

SANTA CLARA, Calif., Nov. 10, 2026 – AMD (NASDAQ: AMD) today announced the general availability of the 6th Gen AMD EPYC™ server SP7 processors, based on the new “Zen 6” architecture, extending its historical server CPU performance leadership as AI creates new demands across the data center. Systems powered by the new CPUs are shipping from all leading server vendors, and cloud instances from Microsoft Azure and OCI are coming soon.

...

##

...

Systems powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC server processors are shipping from leading server vendors:

- Meta is working with AMD as a lead customer and has been validating 6th Gen AMD EPYC CPU-based platforms as the companies prepare for deployment at scale.
- Microsoft Azure is bringing 6th Gen AMD EPYC to customers across the AI infrastructure stack, with Azure HDv2 now in preview for AI data processing, agentic AI and HPC; Azure HXv2 for EDA and technical computing; and Azure ND MI455X v7, based on AMD Helios, for production-scale AI inference.
- AMD recently shared updates to its multigeneration collaboration with Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). OCI Compute E7 cloud compute instances will be powered by 6th Gen AMD EPYC server processors, supporting enterprise applications and the CPU services surrounding AI models.

title: AMD launches Zen 6 Epyc 9006 series with up to 256 cores, 512 threads, and TSMC N2 | TechSpot
text:
# AMD launches Zen 6 Epyc 9006 series with up to 256 cores, 512 threads, and TSMC N2

## Pricing starts at $700 for an eight-core part, while the top chip reportedly costs $14,904

 By Daniel Sims November 11, 2026, 0:06 9 Add TS 

Highly anticipated: AMD has fully pulled back the curtain on its first Zen 6 CPU lineup. Debuting with Epyc server chips, the new architecture offers up to 256 cores and 512 threads at the top end, and AMD has promised substantial upgrades in AI, GPU hosting, and per-watt performance. 

AMD's first Zen 6 Epyc processors, labeled the 9006 series and codenamed Venice, are now shipping to server clients, with SP7 systems arriving first and SP8 following in the first half of 2027. The company recently published the full technical specs for every SP7 and SP8 CPU in the lineup, mainly promoting their usefulness for AI workloads.

As expected, AMD's new flagship Epyc 9996 raises the maximum core count to 256, with 512 threads, clocked at up to 4.1GHz. With 1GB of L3 cache, it sits at a 2.55GHz base clock and defaults to 600W, though it can be configured down to 400W.

AMD's rack-density comparisons also reference a 400W, 256-core 9956, but that chip isn't on the published list. According to AMD's internal benchmarks, the 9996 at least doubles the Intel Xeon 6980P's performance in some tasks and more than triples it in others.

Early independent testing backs up the scale of the gains: Tom's Hardware measured a dual 9996 server at up to 93% faster than a dual Epyc 9965 in SPEC CPU 2026's intrate test. AMD lists the top-end chip at $14,904, but the lineup also scales all the way down to the eight-core, 16-thread Epyc 9016, at just $700.

AMD's Ryzen 7 9800X3D returns to $399.99, matching a previous in-store promotion.

## Newegg cuts Ryzen 7 9800X3D to $399.99

AMD’s Ryzen 7 9800X3D has finally returned below $400 in the US. # AMD Reveals Not Terrible Pricing for Ryzen 9000 [Value Analysis]

AMD has officially confirmed the pricing for its highly anticipated Ryzen 9000 series, revealing that the Zen 5 processors will launch at lower MSRPs than the previous generation. Starting at just $279 for the Ryzen 5 9600X and topping out at $649 for the flagship Ryzen 9 9950X, AMD is making a clear play for market dominance by offering superior efficiency at a more accessible price point.

...

## Official Ryzen 9000 MSRP Breakdown

The AMD Ryzen 9000 series is priced between $279 and $649, representing a $20 to $50 reduction across most tiers compared to the Ryzen 7000 launch.

This aggressive pricing strategy marks a significant shift in the competitive landscape. By lowering the entry barrier for the Zen 5 architecture, AMD is signaling a desire to saturate the market quickly and move users onto the AM5 platform.

The pricing tiers reflect a calculated effort to maintain high-authority performance standards without the sticker shock typical of new flagship silicon. Enthusiasts and professional creators alike will find the lower MSRPs particularly enticing given the current economic climate.

This strategic price reduction positions AMD aggressively against Intel's current high-end offerings. By lowering the entry barrier, AMD is effectively capitalizing on market demand for stable and affordable high-performance computing.

### When is the Ryzen 9000 release date?

The Ryzen 9600X and 9700X are scheduled for release on August 8, 2024, followed by the 9900X and 9950X on August 15, 2024.

This staggered launch allows AMD to address the mid-range market first before rolling out its flagship enthusiast chips. It ensures a steady supply chain and focused marketing for each tier of the Zen 5 architecture.

# Intel, Qualcomm, and AMD are reportedly raising CPU prices one after another.

13/11/2026

Supply chain sources say Intel has taken the lead in raising prices for several PC processors since September, with high-end Panther Lake chips seeing increases of 15% to 20%, while Meteor Lake and Arrow Lake rose about 5% to 10%. Panther Lake did not see across-the-board price increases; this round of adjustments was concentrated on products manufactured by TSMC's N3E process and equipped with high-end GPU tiles. Platforms such as Qualcomm's Snapdragon X/X2 Elite saw price increases of about 10% starting in October. AMD is also reported to be preparing to adjust prices for some CPUs, with the extent, scope, and effective timing of the increases still to be confirmed.

title: AMD introduces Epyc 6 processors for AI agent workloads - SiliconANGLE | hamster.news
text:
# AMD introduces Epyc 6 processors for AI agent workloads - SiliconANGLE

AMD Processors 11 lis 2026, 00:20· Hardware News

11 November 2026· 2 min read

Advanced Micro Devices Inc. has introduced the Epyc 6 series server processors, optimized for AI agent workloads and offering performance improvements over competitors.

At a glance

AMD's new Epyc 6 chips, built on a 2nm process with Zen 6 architecture, can support up to 3.3 more AI agents per watt than Nvidia's Vera CPU and outperform comparable Intel processors. The processors are already being used by major data center suppliers and Microsoft Azure.

The Epyc 6 series, also known as Venice, comprises 10 CPUs organized into two groups. The first set includes chips with many relatively slow cores, while the remaining CPUs feature fewer, higher-frequency cores. Both collections feature optimizations designed to speed up artificial intelligence agents.

...

The two highest frequency Epyc 6 chips have a base speed of 4.05 GHz and can boost to 5.3 GHz for demanding workloads. Both chips have 96 cores and a 384-megabyte cache. The two densest chips include 256 cores with a base speed of 2.55 GHz, enabling 512 threads for running numerous AI agents simultaneously.

Deploying AI agent tools on CPUs with fewer cores can reduce software expenses in some cases. Certain enterprise applications, notably databases, are billed according to the number of cores, making deployment on one high-frequency core cheaper than using two slower ones with equivalent processing power.

...

AMD reports that major data center suppliers have already begun shipping servers equipped with Epyc 6 chips. The processors also power Microsoft Azure instances optimized for AI inference workloads and chip design software, indicating strong early adoption in the enterprise market.
